product_owner_answers.create_contract: POST /holds accepts seat_id, customer_id, idempotency_key, and optional ttl_seconds. TTL defaults to 120 seconds and must be 1 through 900.
product_owner_answers.create_result: First creation returns 201. An identical retry with the same idempotency key returns the same hold without extending expiry and may return 200 or 201 if documented consistently.
product_owner_answers.idempotency_conflict: Reusing an idempotency key with a different request returns 409.
product_owner_answers.states: ACTIVE, CONFIRMED, CANCELLED, EXPIRED. Expiry is based on an injected UTC clock and is observed lazily on reads or mutations.
product_owner_answers.seat_exclusivity: Only one ACTIVE hold can exist per seat. A CONFIRMED hold permanently consumes the seat in this service. CANCELLED or EXPIRED holds release it.
product_owner_answers.operations: GET /holds/{hold_id} reads current state; POST /holds/{hold_id}/confirm confirms; DELETE /holds/{hold_id} cancels and returns 204 on the first successful cancellation.
product_owner_answers.state_conflicts: Confirming expired or cancelled, cancelling confirmed, or acting on an unknown hold returns a clear 404 or 409 according to the documented contract; no transition silently succeeds.
product_owner_answers.concurrency: Two simultaneous create requests for the same free seat and different idempotency keys result in exactly one ACTIVE hold and one 409.

acceptance.criterion: Create validates required fields and TTL range, persists to SQLite, and returns a documented representation with stable id, state, created_at, and expires_at.
Identical idempotent replay returns the original hold without extending expiry; key reuse with different payload returns 409.
A controllable UTC clock drives lazy ACTIVE to EXPIRED transition exactly at expiry, and an expired hold releases the seat.
Confirm and cancel enforce the state machine; confirmed seats remain unavailable and invalid transitions return documented errors.
A real concurrent create race against one SQLite database yields one success, one 409, and never two ACTIVE holds.
Restarting the app against the same database preserves holds and idempotency outcomes.
OpenAPI and handoff document exact endpoints, status codes, state meanings, clock-test mechanism, install, run, and test commands.

robustness: Malformed JSON and invalid TTL return 422 without partial writes.
SQLite lock handling does not surface an unhandled 500 in the required two-request race.
Unknown ids and illegal transitions have stable structured errors.
api_review: Names and status codes are internally consistent.
The representation makes state and expiry unambiguous.
Operational setup avoids hidden global state and runtime database artifacts in source.
